design_clause: G1 — proposal coverage. On a preregistered plain-question set committed before the proposer exists: what fraction of utterances yield at least one verified candidate?
committed_before: the proposer, the candidate enumerator, and any model call from this lane. This file's commit is an ancestor of theirs and a test asks git.
the_population_this_set_names: thirty plain-English questions written BY THE MAINTAINER, ABOUT THIS CORPUS, in one sitting, before the proposer existed. That is the whole population and no larger one is claimed.
the_warning_inherited_verbatim: Questions a maintainer wrote about this corpus are not questions a stranger asks; **STRANGER**'s park (`docs/ROADMAP-v0.20.md:394`) is the same fresh-half problem and should be cited, not re-encountered.
so_the_denominator_says: a rate measured here is a rate over maintainer-authored questions about a corpus the author knows. It is not a coverage claim about plain English, about strangers, or about questions nobody wrote down.
the_set_is_not_stacked_and_here_is_the_p: 9 of the 30 are authored to EXHAUST — they are outside the corpus, or not questions with an exact answer at all, and the honest reply to them is a refusal. A question set on which everything is supposed to work is a set chosen to read well, and this one cannot read better than 21/30 without the proposer inventing something.
authors_prior_is_published_but_is_not_gr: each question carries `authors_prior`, the disposition the author expected before anything ran. It is preregistered so the run can DISAGREE with it visibly. It is NOT a correctness key: G1 measures the verified-candidate fraction, and agreement with the prior is reported beside it as a second number with this caveat attached.

dispositions.conditional: the author expects exactly one candidate to verify with a framing variable left unresolved
dispositions.ask: the author expects two or more candidates to verify
dispositions.exhaust: the author expects no candidate to verify, and a refusal is the honest answer

non_claims: no stranger-usability claim: these are maintainer-authored
no coverage claim about plain English: the denominator is these thirty questions
the authors_prior is a published expectation, not a correctness key
counts_note: computed from the questions themselves, not typed beside them. The first version of this file typed 16/6/8 against an actual 17/5/8 — the same class of defect slice 1's review found five times, caught here by the suite before the artifact was committed.

ceiling.why: the exhaust-prior questions have no committed material to verify against, so a candidate that verified for one of them would be the proposer inventing rather than selecting.

counts_note_correction.found_by: adversarial review of the slice-2 merge candidate
counts_note_correction.the_sentence_corrected: `counts_note` reads "The first version of this file typed 16/6/8 against an actual 17/5/8". The actual is **16/5/9** — conditional 16, ask 5, exhaust 9 — which is what the `counts` block beside it has always carried and what the suite has always checked.
counts_note_correction.why_the_original_sentence_is_left_where_: the file is a SEALED input set whose commit is an ancestor of every proposer commit, and the `counts` block is computed from the questions rather than typed. Rewriting the prose would edit a sealed artifact to fix a sentence about a defect; adding the correction beside it leaves the seal checkable and the mistake legible.
counts_note_correction.and_the_irony_is_the_point: `counts_note` is the field that congratulates the suite for catching a typed count, and it typed a count. No number this set is used for moves: every denominator in the run is read from `counts` or recomputed from `questions`, and a test now asserts the corrected triple against both.
